title: Supported Cartier Kummer map for ordinary etale arbitrary finite coefficients
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $N\geq1$ be invertible on $T$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$. Let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ be an effective Cartier divisor: its ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and let $j:T\setminus D\hookrightarrow T$ be its open complement. Use the ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and the twist $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$ of [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. The line bundle $\mathcal O_T(D)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] with its canonical trivialization off $D$ has a supported Kummer boundary for the exact sequence of [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. This boundary determines a canonical morphism
$$c_{D,A}:Ri_*A_D\longrightarrow A_T(1)[2].$$
If $u_D:A_T\longrightarrow Ri_*A_D$ is the inverse-image/direct-image unit, then $c_{D,A}u_D=c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$, where $c_1$ is the Kummer boundary followed by derived scalar extension from $\mathbf Z/N$ to $A$. For every morphism $v:T'\to T$ whose scheme-theoretic pullback $D'=T'\times_TD$ remains an effective Cartier divisor, the canonical closed-immersion exchange identifies $v^{-1}c_{D,A}$ with $c_{D',A}$. The map is the derived scalar extension of $c_{D,\mathbf Z/N}$, using the canonical identifications of its source and target with $Ri_*A_D$ and $A_T(1)[2]$.

proof.text: Put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/N$ and $V=T-D$. The dual ideal $L$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] has a canonical section $s_D$, dual to $\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T$. On an open chart where $\mathcal I_D=(f_a)$ with $f_a$ a nonzerodivisor, the ideal is free on $f_a$, its dual is free on $e_a=f_a^{-1}$, and $s_D=f_ae_a$. On $V=T-D$, $f_a$ is a unit, so $s_D$ is a nowhere zero section and gives a specified trivialization $\tau_D:\mathcal O_V\cong L|_V$. On overlaps $e_b=(f_a/f_b)e_a$, hence these formulas agree. The frame torsor $P_D=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_T,L)$ of [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor] is therefore a $\mathbf G_m$-torsor with the specified section $\tau_D$ on $V$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: divisor section and trivialization

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] to $(P_D,\tau_D)$ with $G=\mathbf G_m$. This gives a specified class $\alpha_D\in H^1(T,V;\mathbf G_m)$, independent of chart equations and refinements, whose forgotten-support image is the torsor class of $L$. For explicit changes of equations, $f'_a=u_af_a$ gives $e'_a=u_a^{-1}e_a$ and $f'_ae'_a=f_ae_a$; it is the same line bundle with the same section, not just an unspecified lift of its Picard class. The relative lemma supplies the comparison with derived sections; no assertion that an arbitrary ordinary Cech cover computes all derived cohomology is needed.

Since $N$ is invertible on $T$, [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] supplies the short exact Kummer sequence $0\to\mu_N\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{N}\mathbf G_m\to0$. Apply its relative connecting map, provided by [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], to $\alpha_D$: $\beta_D=\delta_{T,V}(\alpha_D)\in H^2(T,V;\mu_N)$. The relative lemma's compatibility with forgetting support gives $\operatorname{forget}(\beta_D)=\delta_T([L])$, exactly $c_{1,\Lambda}(L)$. Only the abelian-sheaf Kummer sequence is used: $\mathbf G_m$ is not a $\Lambda$-module and is never tensored over $\Lambda$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: Kummer boundary; Stacks Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence

proof.text: Use the canonical comparisons from module-derived sections to abelian-derived sections for the sheaf $\mu_N$ on $T$ and its restriction on $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget] they induce isomorphisms on every cohomology group, hence are quasi-isomorphisms. They commute with restriction because both restriction maps send a section to its restriction. Taking their cones therefore identifies $H^2(T,V;\mu_N)$ with the relative cohomology computed in $\Lambda$-module sheaves; the projection from the shifted cone to the $T$-sections complex also commutes with these comparisons. Taking degree two in [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], with coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and $K=\mu_N[0]$, identifies it with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)}(i_*\Lambda_D,\mu_{N,T}[2])$. Define $c_{D,\Lambda}$ to be the morphism corresponding to $\beta_D$. The forget-support map is precomposition with $\Lambda_T\to i_*\Lambda_D$: applying derived Hom to this map is the first arrow into the ordinary sections complex in the support cone. Thus step 3 is precisely the required first Chern class assertion. This is a support-Hom identification and uses no purity isomorphism. The forget-support compatibility can be checked directly using [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] for $F=\Lambda_T$. Apply derived Hom into $\mu_N$ to $j_!\Lambda_V\to\Lambda_T\to i_*\Lambda_D$. [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] identifies Hom out of $j_!\Lambda_V$ with sections on $V$, and the counit induces restriction. Thus the relative fibre projects to sections on $T$ by precomposition with the displayed unit. This fixes the maps, not just an abstract isomorphism of cohomology groups.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 3-4: support-Hom; Stacks Tag 0A45, lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is finite: locally it is induced by a quotient ring, generated by $1$ as a module. [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] gives exactness of $i_*$ on abelian sheaves. Kernels and sheafified cokernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] have their underlying abelian kernels and cokernels, so $i_*$ is also exact on constant-coefficient module sheaves. Hence $Ri_*\Lambda_D=i_*\Lambda_D$ and $Ri_*A_D=i_*A_D$ for these degree-zero objects. Apply the exact derived change-of-rings functor [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] along $\Lambda_T\to A_T$ to $c_{D,\Lambda}$. Its source is canonically $i_*A_D$: [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] computes the stalks of $i_*\Lambda_D$ as $\Lambda$ on $D$ and zero off $D$; [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], and [lem-kun-pullback-constant] compute its derived tensor with $A_T$ as respectively $\Lambda\otimes^L_\Lambda A=A$ and zero. The canonical comparison to $i_*A_D$, induced by scalar multiplication and adjunction, is the identity on these stalks. Exact stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and conservative stalks [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] imply that every cohomology sheaf of its cone vanishes. The target is $(\mu_{N,T}\otimes^L_\Lambda A_T)[2]$. Apply [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] with $A=\Lambda$: $\mu_{N,T}$ is a flat $\Lambda_T$-line. Its degree-zero complex is K-flat because the exact tensor functor preserves kernels and images and therefore acyclicity. The K-flat computation of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies this target with the ordinary tensor $A_T(1)[2]$. Define $c_{D,A}$ as the extended map under these canonical isomorphisms. The same stalk calculation sends $\Lambda_T\to i_*\Lambda_D$ to $u_D:A_T\to i_*A_D$. Applying scalar extension to the equality of step 4 gives $c_{D,A}u_D=c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$, with exactly the stated scalar-extended Kummer definition of $c_1$. This proves the scalar-extension clause as well. No flatness of $A$ over $\Lambda$ is required.

source.place: Proof last paragraph: derived scalar extension; Stacks Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product

proof.text: Let $h:T'\to T$ and assume $D'$ is Cartier. Pull the above charts back: $f'_a=h^*f_a$ generates the pulled-back ideal and is a nonzerodivisor by this assumption, Indeed locally $(f'_a)=(g)$ for a regular generator $g$, so writing $f'_a=ag$ and $g=bf'_a$ gives $ba=1$ by cancellation of $g$; hence $a$ is a unit and $f'_a$ is regular. Thus $e'_a=(f'_a)^{-1}$ is its dual basis. The transition equality $e'_b=h^*(f_a/f_b)e'_a$ and section equality $s_{D'}=f'_ae'_a$ identify $(h^*L,h^*s_D)$ with $(\mathcal O_{T'}(D'),s_{D'})$. This computation requires no flatness of $h$. Pullback of the frame torsor is taken with the coefficient map $h^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,T}\to\mathbf G_{m,T'}$, not an assumed isomorphism of those two sheaves. Naturality of the relative torsor class and of its connecting maps in [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] now sends $\alpha_D$ and $\beta_D$ to $\alpha_{D'}$ and $\beta_{D'}$: the maps of Kummer sequences send $u$ to its pulled-back unit and satisfy $h^*(u^N)=h^*(u)^N$. The canonical map $h^{-1}\mu_{N,T}\to\mu_{N,T'}$ is an isomorphism. Use [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] with $A=\Lambda$ to choose an etale cover with a primitive-root generator. On its pulled-back cover the same root is a generator: the factorization of $X^N-1$ into its distinct root factors, with invertible pairwise differences, pulls back to the identical factorization. Thus the map is the identity on the two constant rank-one $\Lambda$-modules there. For $N=1$ both are zero. Apply the natural support-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]; its source comparison $h^{-1}i_*\Lambda_D\to i'_*\Lambda_{D'}$ is the identity $\Lambda\to\Lambda$ on the pulled-back support and $0\to0$ elsewhere by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] and [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], so is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] applies these comparisons to complexes and their cohomology sheaves. Finally [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] and [lem-kun-pullback-constant] identify the pullback of derived extension to $A$ with derived extension after pullback. All these comparison maps are the indicated unit or tensor maps, so their naturality applies to the morphism, giving $h^{-1}c_{D,A}=c_{D',A}$, including equality after forgetting support. For clarity, the support-Hom naturality used here is the canonical relative-fibre comparison of step 4: pulling back a morphism $i_*\Lambda_D\to K[2]$ and precomposing with inverse closed exchange induces pullback on sections on $T$ and $V$, since each comparison carries the constant generator $1$ to $1$. The map on relative fibres is therefore exactly the pullback used on $\beta_D$, giving equality of supported morphisms, not only their images after forgetting support. The exact module inverse image of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] preserves the open-closed triangle of step 4. Finally the derived tensor comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] applied with the constant $\Lambda$-complex $A$, and [lem-kun-pullback-constant], give the scalar-extension comparison. On the flat roots-of-unity target this is the ordinary tensor comparison of step 5. All maps are the specified adjunction, unit and tensor maps, so substituting these comparisons into the definition of $c_{D,A}$ gives the asserted equality for $A$.
